title: Surrounded Regions
pattern: Flood-fill from the border, then flip the rest
statement: Given a board of `X` and `O`, **capture** every region of `O`s that is completely surrounded by `X` (on all four sides) by flipping those `O`s to `X`. A region that touches the border of the board can not be captured. Modify the board in place.

example.why: The three O's in the middle are enclosed and get flipped. The O in the bottom row touches the border, so it survives.

idea: Deciding directly whether a region is surrounded is awkward. The opposite is easy: an `O` is **safe** exactly when it is connected to an `O` on the border.
So start a flood-fill from every border `O` and mark everything it reaches with a temporary letter `E` (*escaped*).
Afterwards every `O` that is still an `O` was never reached from the border — flip it to `X`. Turn the `E` marks back into `O`.

complexity.timeWhy: Each cell is visited a constant number of times.
complexity.spaceWhy: Recursion depth in the worst case (a board full of connected O's).
